questions: Should the random float be generated by interpreting 4 random bytes as a float (e.g., struct.unpack), or should it be a random float from a range (e.g., random.uniform) that is then converted to 4 bytes?
Is the float in big-endian or little-endian byte order when converting to bytes?
Should the base64 encoding use the standard alphabet (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, /) or a URL-safe variant (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, -, _)?
Should the base64 output include padding characters (=) or be stripped of them?
Is the output expected to be ASCII-encoded (as in the reference solution) or raw bytes?
Should the function generate a new random float on each call, or can it be deterministic (e.g., seeded)?
Is the float intended to be a valid IEEE 754 single-precision float, or any 4-byte sequence?
Should the base64 encoding be performed directly on the 4 bytes (as in reference) or on a hexadecimal string derived from those bytes?
